by_owasp.name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows

findings.title: Concurrent payments bypass daily limit and lose balance updates

owasp.name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows

findings.description: Balance and spend-limit checks are separated from their writes by an await, so simultaneous payments all observe the same stale state and overwrite each other's deductions.
findings.impact: A teen can approve more payments than the daily allowance allows, spend the balance multiple times, and move the ledger out of sync with the wallet.

evidence.notes: 12/12 concurrent payments approved (safe maximum 1); wallet moved by 3000 cents for 36000 cents of approved volume.

remediation.summary: Make each invariant a single conditional UPDATE in one transaction, or lock the wallet row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) before reading it.
remediation.vulnerable:
balance = wallet.balance_cents
if balance < amount:
    raise HTTPException(402)
await asyncio.sleep(RACE_WINDOW)
wallet.balance_cents = balance - amount
db.commit()
remediation.secure:
spend_ok = db.execute(
    update(Allowance)
    .where(Allowance.teen_id == teen.id)
    .where(Allowance.spent_today_cents + amount <= Allowance.daily_limit_cents)
    .values(spent_today_cents=Allowance.spent_today_cents + amount)
)
if spend_ok.rowcount != 1:
    db.rollback()
    raise HTTPException(403, "daily limit exceeded")
balance_ok = db.execute(
    update(Wallet)
    .where(Wallet.teen_id == teen.id, Wallet.balance_cents >= amount)
    .values(balance_cents=Wallet.balance_cents - amount)
)

findings.title: Cross-tenant allowance takeover (BOLA write)
findings.description: Parent A can rewrite another family's allowance and reassign it to their own parent id by calling the allowance endpoint with a foreign teen_id.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled guardian can lift spending limits and merchant-category blocks for any teen, defeating the core control of the neobank.

evidence.notes: Parent A set Teen B's limit to 999999 cents and cleared the MCC blocklist.

remediation.summary: Never trust teen_id from the request body. Resolve the teen through a query constrained by parent_id before mutating anything.
remediation.vulnerable:
teen = _teen_or_404(db, payload.teen_id)
allowance = db.get(Allowance, teen.id)
allowance.daily_limit_cents = payload.daily_limit_cents
allowance.blocked_mccs = json.dumps(payload.blocked_mccs)
db.commit()
remediation.secure:
teen = db.scalar(
    select(User)
    .where(User.id == payload.teen_id)
    .where(User.parent_id == parent.id)
    .where(User.role == "teen")
)
if teen is None:
    raise HTTPException(404, "teen not found in your family")
allowance.daily_limit_cents = payload.daily_limit_cents

findings.title: Merchant category block bypass via MCC array smuggling

owasp.name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows

findings.description: The payment endpoint checks the first MCC in a supplied list but books the last one, so a blocked category can be disguised as an allowed one.
findings.impact: A teen can spend against a parent-blocked category (for example gambling, MCC 7995) while the authorization decision sees grocery (5411).

evidence.notes: Policy evaluated mcc[0]=5411 (grocery) but booked mcc[-1]=7995 (gambling).

remediation.summary: Reject list values for a scalar field, normalize once, and authorize the exact MCC that will be persisted.

findings.title: Cross-tenant allowance disclosure (BOLA)
findings.description: Parent A can read the allowance configuration of a teen in another family by supplying that teen's identifier.
findings.impact: Discloses another household's spending limits and blocked merchant categories, enabling targeted policy-evasion attempts.

evidence.notes: Parent A read allowance owned by usr_teen_b (usr_parent_b)

remediation.summary: Scope the lookup by both resource id and authenticated parent id, and return 404 when the pair does not match.
remediation.vulnerable:
teen = db.get(User, teen_id)
allowance = db.get(Allowance, teen.id)
return allowance  # authenticated parent never compared

findings.title: Cross-tenant SIM-binding disclosure
findings.description: A parent can read the SIM serial and attestation profile bound to another family's teen device.
findings.impact: SIM serials and attestation strength are the exact inputs needed to social-engineer a carrier swap or forge a device assertion.

evidence.notes: Response includes the SIM serial and attestation profile for Teen B.

remediation.summary: Apply the same ownership predicate to device lookups and strip serial numbers from responses not needed by the client.
remediation.vulnerable:
device = db.get(Device, teen_id)
return _device_payload(device)  # no family scoping

findings.title: Cross-tenant transaction history disclosure
findings.description: Parent A can list the payment history of another family's teen.
findings.impact: Exposes merchant names, amounts and MCCs of minors outside the authenticated household.

evidence.notes: Parent A listed another household's transaction history.

remediation.summary: Derive the teen id from the authenticated relationship instead of the path, or validate parent ownership first.
